threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Seeing someone eating their dinner on the 394 bus like it’s the most normal thing in the world. Welcome to the chaos, mate.
Caught the 333 last night, and a guy in a full tuxedo was chatting about his lost cufflink like it was the end of the world. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids using a broken lamppost as a makeshift basketball hoop in Körnerpark. Pure Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a spontaneous rave in a U-Bahn tunnel when the trains stop running. It’s the wildest form of public transport rebellion.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell the locals—they're the ones who can name the best taco spot without Googling and know the bus schedule by heart, delays and all.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Was on the 47 when it came to a halt because someone’s emotional support iguana decided to sunbathe on the tracks. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into a bar and order a 'mojito' like it's the norm. Here, it's all about vermut and cerveza. mojitos are for the beach.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still struggle with the whole 'café con leche' vs. 'latte' thing – you can spot them fumbling at the bar counter.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 73 bus will be reliable; everyone else has a backup plan since it's always late or just doesn't show.
Saw a guy on the N37 serenading the whole bus with old reggae tunes. Everyone was surprisingly into it; even the driver tapped the steering wheel.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid in a dirndl selling homemade pretzels outside the Späti during Oktoberfest. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a techno club in an old slaughterhouse, where the beats drop harder than the temperature outside in February.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local when they can navigate the pothole minefield on 16th without missing a beat, but tourists are out here dodging like it’s a game.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I saw a guy serenading Muni riders with a ukulele at Civic Center—complete with an impromptu dance from an elderly lady. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's just about the parks and plazas, but the real charm is in the back streets where the locals chat over morning coffee, not selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they stand in line at the bakery for a whole baguette instead of just asking for a ‘barra’.
